title: ITR-3 & ITR-4: Key Schedules and Verification for AY 2026-27
description: Taxpayers with business or professional income must carefully choose between ITR-3 and ITR-4 based on their income type and turnover. ITR-3 is for individuals.

faq.q: Who is eligible to file ITR-3?
faq.a: ITR-3 is for individuals and Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs) who have income from a proprietary business or profession, or are partners in a firm, along with other income sources like capital gains or house property.

faq.q: What is the main difference between ITR-3 and ITR-4?
faq.a: ITR-3 is for taxpayers with business or professional income who maintain detailed books of account or are not eligible for presumptive taxation. ITR-4 (Sugam) is a simplified form for small taxpayers opting for the presumptive taxation scheme under Sections 44AD, 44ADA, or 44AE, avoiding the need for detailed bookkeeping.

faq.q: How do I reconcile my income with Form 26AS and AIS?
faq.a: Download both documents from the Income Tax e-filing portal. Compare all income entries (salary, interest, professional fees, etc.) and TDS/TCS entries in your ITR with those reflected in Form 26AS and AIS. Address any discrepancies by correcting your ITR or contacting the deductor.

faq.q: Can I file ITR-4 if my business turnover is ₹3 crores?
faq.a: No, you cannot. ITR-4 under Section 44AD is applicable only if your gross business turnover does not exceed ₹2 crores. For a turnover of ₹3 crores, you would typically need to file ITR-3 and maintain proper books of account.

faq.q: What if I forgot to claim a TDS entry in my ITR?
faq.a: If you forgot to claim a valid TDS entry that is reflected in your Form 26AS, you might receive a tax demand. You can file a revised return (if within the permissible time limit) to claim the TDS credit.

faq.q: Is it mandatory to maintain books of account for ITR-4?
faq.a: No, one of the primary benefits of opting for presumptive taxation under ITR-4 is that you are not required to maintain detailed books of account as specified under Section 44AA of the Income Tax Act.

faq.q: What is the deadline for filing ITR for individuals with business income?
faq.a: For individuals and HUFs whose accounts are not required to be audited, the deadline for filing ITR (including ITR-3 and ITR-4) for AY 2026-27 (FY 2025-26) is typically July 31st. However, the prompt mentions August 31st, which could be an extended deadline for the current year or specific cases. Always refer to the latest notifications from the Income Tax Department for the exact due date.
